does not depend on `ℓ`, so for positive `N`, `Fcal`, `σ₀` and atomic data the map
`ℓ ↦ thickLineIntensity` is strictly decreasing on `ℓ > 0`. A real homogeneous column emits
more when it is longer; the model matches that only when `Fcal` (which lumps the emitting
volume) is scaled with `ℓ`. Results that fix `ℓ` are unaffected.

Relation REDUCED (homogeneous single-temperature slab, flat line-center cross-section);
publishes APPROXIMATION via `selfAbsorbedIntensity`.
type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] {kB T N Fcal sigma0 : ℝ} {g E A : ι → ℝ},
  (∀ (k : ι), (0 : ℝ) < g k) →
    (0 : ℝ) < N →
      (0 : ℝ) < Fcal →
        (∀ (k : ι), (0 : ℝ) < A k) →
          (0 : ℝ) < sigma0 →
            ∀ (u l : ι),
              StrictAntiOn
                (fun ell ↦ CflibsFormal.thickLineIntensity kB T N Fcal sigma0 ell g E A u l)
                (Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ))

name: CflibsFormal.thickLineIntensity_strictMonoOn
docstring:
**The absorption channel is strictly monotone in density.** Once `τ` is bound to `N`,
the MEASURED (self-absorbed) intensity is STRICTLY INCREASING in `N` on `(0, ∞)`. Neither
factor gives this on its own: the thin intensity is linear in `N` but the escape factor
`SA(τ(N))` is strictly *decreasing* in `N`; their product `S·(1 − exp(−τ(N)))` is strictly
increasing because the source strength `S` is `N`-free.

Relation REDUCED (homogeneous single-temperature slab, flat line-center cross-section);
publishes APPROXIMATION via `selfAbsorbedIntensity`.
type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] {kB T Fcal sigma0 ell : ℝ} {g E A : ι → ℝ},
  (∀ (k : ι), (0 : ℝ) < g k) →
    (0 : ℝ) < Fcal →
      (∀ (k : ι), (0 : ℝ) < A k) →
        (0 : ℝ) < sigma0 →
          (0 : ℝ) < ell →
            ∀ (u l : ι),
              StrictMonoOn
                (fun N ↦ CflibsFormal.thickLineIntensity kB T N Fcal sigma0 ell g E A u l)
                (Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ))

name: CflibsFormal.thickObserve
docstring:
**Optically-thick observation map.** The self-absorption-aware analogue of
`Inverse.observe`: the observable for species `s` is the **measured** (self-absorbed)
intensity of its single emitting line `emit s` at per-line optical depth `tau s`, reusing
`SelfAbsorption.selfAbsorbedIntensity` verbatim — so it inherits that definition's
flat-profile model (model tag APPROXIMATION). When `tau ≡ 0` this collapses to
`Inverse.observe`, since `SA 0 = 1`.
type:
{species : Type u_1} →
  {levelIndex : Type u_2} →
    [Fintype levelIndex] →
      ℝ →
        ℝ →
          (species → levelIndex) →
            (species → ℝ) → CflibsFormal.PlasmaParams species levelIndex → species → ℝ

name: CflibsFormal.thick_composition_identifiability
docstring:
**PRESERVED (known, matched `τ`) — multi-species composition identifiability.** With
shared `T`, calibration `Fcal`, and atomic data `g E A`, if two admissible parameter sets
produce equal **measured** thick spectra at **matched, known** optical depths `tau`, then
they have equal closure composition. Per line the known `SA(tau s)` cancels (via
`thick_density_identifiability`), giving equal `N s` for every species, hence equal
`trueComposition`. The direct self-absorption analogue of `general_identifiability`'s
composition conclusion; `T` equality is supplied honestly (one line per species cannot pin
`T`), and `tau` being matched/known is precisely the PRESERVED hypothesis. Admissibility of the
second set (`_ha₂`) is stated for symmetry and not used: with the atomic data shared, the first
set's admissibility suffices.

`trueComposition` is the estimator-independent target, so the statement is non-tautological.
type:
∀ {species : Type u_1} {levelIndex : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype species]
  [inst_1 : Fintype levelIndex] [Nonempty levelIndex] {kB Fcal₁ Fcal₂ : ℝ}
  {emit : species → levelIndex} {tau : species → ℝ}
  {p₁ p₂ : CflibsFormal.PlasmaParams species levelIndex},
  p₁.Admissible →
    p₂.Admissible →
      p₁.g = p₂.g →
        p₁.E = p₂.E →
          p₁.A = p₂.A →
            p₁.T = p₂.T →
              (0 : ℝ) < Fcal₁ →
                Fcal₁ = Fcal₂ →
                  (∀ (s : species), (0 : ℝ) ≤ tau s) →
                    CflibsFormal.thickObserve kB Fcal₁ emit tau p₁ =
                        CflibsFormal.thickObserve kB Fcal₂ emit tau p₂ →
                      ∀ (s : species),
                        CflibsFormal.trueComposition p₁ s = CflibsFormal.trueComposition p₂ s

name: CflibsFormal.thick_density_identifiability
docstring:
**PRESERVED (known, matched `τ`) — per-species density identifiability.** If two
densities produce equal **measured** thick intensities of the same line at the **same**
known optical depth `tau`, then the densities are equal. The known positive `SA(tau)`
cancels, reducing to the proven thin `density_identifiability`. This is the model left-inverse
(`lineIntensity_eq_selfAbsorbedIntensity_div`) made injective: within the flat-profile model,
self-absorption is invertible when its optical depth is known and matched.
type:
∀ {ι : Type u_3} [inst : Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] {kB T Fcal : ℝ} {g E A : ι → ℝ} {N₁ N₂ : ℝ},
  (∀ (k : ι), (0 : ℝ) < g k) →
    (0 : ℝ) < Fcal →
      ∀ (u : ι),
        (0 : ℝ) < A u →
          ∀ {tau : ℝ},
            (0 : ℝ) ≤ tau →
              CflibsFormal.selfAbsorbedIntensity kB T N₁ Fcal g E A u tau =
                  CflibsFormal.selfAbsorbedIntensity kB T N₂ Fcal g E A u tau →
                N₁ = N₂

name: CflibsFormal.tiltMean
docstring:
**Tilted mean inverse temperature at the anchor energy `a`**:
`⟨b⟩_a = ∑ z, tiltWeight w b a z · b z`. This — not the arithmetic mean of `b`, and not the
reciprocal of any volume-averaged temperature — is the quantity the apparent Boltzmann
temperature bounds.
type: {ζ : Type u_1} → [Fintype ζ] → (ζ → ℝ) → (ζ → ℝ) → ℝ → ℝ

name: CflibsFormal.tiltMean_homogeneous
docstring:
If every mixed state shares one inverse temperature `β`, the tilted mean collapses to `β`
at every anchor energy. Without this the temperature bound `pairSlope_le_tiltMean` could still
be slack in the homogeneous limit: it is what makes `apparentBeta_eq_homogeneous` a *sharpness*
statement about that bound rather than about the left-hand side alone.
type:
∀ {ζ : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ζ] [Nonempty ζ] {w b : ζ → ℝ},
  (∀ (z : ζ), (0 : ℝ) < w z) →
    ∀ {beta : ℝ}, (∀ (z : ζ), b z = beta) → ∀ (a : ℝ), CflibsFormal.tiltMean w b a = beta

name: CflibsFormal.tiltMean_le_pairSlope
docstring:
**The mirror bound: the tilted mean at the UPPER line is a lower bound on `β_app`.**
Anchoring the tangent inequality at `E₂` instead of `E₁` and reading it off at `E₁` brackets
the apparent inverse temperature from below, giving `⟨b⟩_{E₂} ≤ β_app ≤ ⟨b⟩_{E₁}`.
type:
∀ {ζ : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ζ] [Nonempty ζ] {w b : ζ → ℝ},
  (∀ (z : ζ), (0 : ℝ) < w z) →
    ∀ {E₁ E₂ : ℝ},
      E₁ < E₂ →
        CflibsFormal.tiltMean w b E₂ ≤
          CflibsFormal.apparentBeta E₁ (CflibsFormal.logMixture w b E₁) E₂
            (CflibsFormal.logMixture w b E₂)

name: CflibsFormal.tiltMean_reweight_le
docstring:
**Antivariant reweighting lowers the tilted mean (PURE-MATH, weighted Chebyshev).** For
positive zone weights `w`, a positive reweight `ρ` that is antivariant with `b`
(`b i < b j → ρ j ≤ ρ i`), and any anchor `a`,
`tiltMean (w·ρ) b a ≤ tiltMean w b a`. Both tilted means are ratios of sums with the common
positive factor `w z e^{−a b z}`; cross-multiplying reduces the claim to the weighted Chebyshev
sum inequality. Equality holds, for example, when `ρ` is constant.
type:
∀ {ζ : Type u_3} [inst : Fintype ζ] [Nonempty ζ] {w b ρ : ζ → ℝ},
  (∀ (z : ζ), (0 : ℝ) < w z) →
    (∀ (z : ζ), (0 : ℝ) < ρ z) →
      (∀ (i j : ζ), b i < b j → ρ j ≤ ρ i) →
        ∀ (a : ℝ), CflibsFormal.tiltMean (fun z ↦ w z * ρ z) b a ≤ CflibsFormal.tiltMean w b a

name: CflibsFormal.tiltWeight
docstring:
**Exponentially tilted weight.** `tiltWeight w b a z = w z e^{−a b z} / M(a)` is zone
`z`'s *fractional share of the observed intensity of the line at energy `a`*. These are
nonnegative and sum to one (`tiltWeight_sum_one`), i.e. they form the tilted probability
measure at anchor `a`.
type: {ζ : Type u_1} → [Fintype ζ] → (ζ → ℝ) → (ζ → ℝ) → ℝ → ζ → ℝ

name: CflibsFormal.tiltWeight_exponent_sum
docstring:
The tilted average of the linear exponent `−(E − a)·b` is `−(E − a)·⟨b⟩_a`. Pure
bookkeeping: it is the step that identifies Jensen's left-hand side with the tangent line.
type:
∀ {ζ : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ζ] (w b : ζ → ℝ) (a E : ℝ),
  ∑ z, CflibsFormal.tiltWeight w b a z * -((E - a) * b z) = -((E - a) * CflibsFormal.tiltMean w b a)

name: CflibsFormal.tiltWeight_mixture
docstring:
Reindexing the mixture through the tilt: `∑ z, p_a(z) · e^{−(E−a) b z} = M(E)/M(a)`.
This is what identifies Jensen's right-hand side with the observed ordinate ratio.
type:
∀ {ζ : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ζ] [Nonempty ζ] {w b : ζ → ℝ},
  (∀ (z : ζ), (0 : ℝ) < w z) →
    ∀ (a E : ℝ),
      ∑ z, CflibsFormal.tiltWeight w b a z * Real.exp (-((E - a) * b z)) =
        CflibsFormal.mixture w b E / CflibsFormal.mixture w b a

name: CflibsFormal.tiltWeight_pos
docstring: Tilted weights are strictly positive.
type:
∀ {ζ : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ζ] [Nonempty ζ] {w b : ζ → ℝ},
  (∀ (z : ζ), (0 : ℝ) < w z) → ∀ (a : ℝ) (z : ζ), (0 : ℝ) < CflibsFormal.tiltWeight w b a z

name: CflibsFormal.tiltWeight_sum_one
docstring:
The tilted weights form a probability vector: they sum to one. This is what licenses
Jensen's inequality against them.
type:
∀ {ζ : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ζ] [Nonempty ζ] {w b : ζ → ℝ},
  (∀ (z : ζ), (0 : ℝ) < w z) → ∀ (a : ℝ), ∑ z, CflibsFormal.tiltWeight w b a z = (1 : ℝ)

name: CflibsFormal.totalDensity
docstring: Total number density `N_tot = ∑ₛ n s` summed over all species/stages `s`.
type: {κ : Type u_1} → [Fintype κ] → (κ → ℝ) → ℝ

name: CflibsFormal.totalDensity_abs_sub_le
docstring:
**Total-density stability (shared CORE).** The total density is stable under a
per-species perturbation bounded by `delta`, with explicit constant `card κ`:
`|N̂_tot - N_tot| ≤ (card κ)·δ`. This is the genuinely new content beyond the
pairwise bounds of `Robustness.lean`, on which the per-fraction and whole-vector
composition bounds rest. Proved by the triangle inequality over the sum.
type:
∀ {κ : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype κ] {N Nhat : κ → ℝ} {delta : ℝ},
  (∀ (s : κ), |Nhat s - N s| ≤ delta) →
    |CflibsFormal.totalDensity Nhat - CflibsFormal.totalDensity N| ≤ ↑(Fintype.card κ) * delta

name: CflibsFormal.totalDensity_pos
docstring:
The total density is positive when at least one species exists and every
species has strictly positive density. Mirrors `partitionFunction_pos`.
type:
∀ {κ : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype κ] [Nonempty κ] {n : κ → ℝ},
  (∀ (s : κ), (0 : ℝ) < n s) → (0 : ℝ) < CflibsFormal.totalDensity n

name: CflibsFormal.totalIntensity
docstring: **Additive measured intensity** at a line pixel: `I_meas = I_line + ε_cont`.
type: ℝ → ℝ → ℝ

name: CflibsFormal.trueComposition
docstring:
The **true composition** of a parameter set: the closure number fractions
`C s = N s / ∑ₜ N t` of the per-species densities, reusing `Closure.composition`.
This is the ground-truth target every sound estimator must return.
type:
{species : Type u_1} →
  {levelIndex : Type u_2} →
    [Fintype species] → CflibsFormal.PlasmaParams species levelIndex → species → ℝ

name: CflibsFormal.twoLevelResidual
docstring:
**Two-level profiled residual as a function of the Boltzmann ratio `t`.** With group energies
`S_A = ∑_{k∈S} (A_k g_k)²`, `S_B = ∑_{k∉S} (A_k g_k)²`, group projections `P = ∑_{k∈S} A_k g_k
obs_k`, `Q = ∑_{k∉S} A_k g_k obs_k`, and `t = exp((E_a − E_b)/(k_B T))`, this is the
`T`-dependent part of the density-profiled least-squares residual (`profiledResidual_twoLevel_eq`).
Its apex is `t* = S_A·Q/(S_B·P)`, where the numerator vanishes.
type: ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ

name: CflibsFormal.twoLevelResidual_diff
docstring:
**Algebraic two-point difference identity for the two-level residual (PURE-MATH, pure `ring`).**
With `u_i := S_B·P·t_i − S_A·Q` (which vanishes at the apex) and `w_i := P + Q·t_i`,
`Ψ(t₂) − Ψ(t₁) = (t₂ − t₁)·(u₁w₂ + u₂w₁) / ((S_A + S_B t₁²)(S_A + S_B t₂²))`.
The `S_A·S_B` normalization cancels exactly. This is the discrete "derivative" that drives the
whole unimodality argument: the sign of the difference is `sign(t₂−t₁)·sign(u₁w₂+u₂w₁)`, so no
calculus, Hessian, or curvature computation is needed anywhere below. It generalizes
`NonlinearLeastSquares.profiledRatioResidual_diff` (recovered at `S_A = S_B = 1`).
type:
∀ {SA SB : ℝ},
  (0 : ℝ) < SA →
    (0 : ℝ) < SB →
      ∀ (P Q t1 t2 : ℝ),
        CflibsFormal.twoLevelResidual SA SB P Q t2 - CflibsFormal.twoLevelResidual SA SB P Q t1 =
          (t2 - t1) *
              ((SB * P * t1 - SA * Q) * (P + Q * t2) + (SB * P * t2 - SA * Q) * (P + Q * t1)) /
            ((SA + SB * t1 ^ (2 : ℕ)) * (SA + SB * t2 ^ (2 : ℕ)))

name: CflibsFormal.twoLineBeta
docstring:
Two-line inverse-temperature (slope) estimate from measured Boltzmann-plot
ordinates `yi = log(I_i/(g_i A_i))`, `yj = log(I_j/(g_j A_j))` at upper-level
energies `Ei`, `Ej`:
  `β = (yj - yi) / (Ei - Ej)`.
This is exactly the slope `1/(k_B T)` recovered by `temperature_from_two_lines`
when `yi`, `yj` are the unperturbed model ordinates (see `boltzmann_plot_intensity`).
Here it is taken as a function of *measured* ordinates so we can bound its
sensitivity to measurement error.
type: ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ

name: CflibsFormal.twoLineBeta_continuous
docstring:
**Continuous dependence.** The recovered inverse-temperature depends continuously
on the observed ordinate pair `(yi, yj)` — a qualitative well-posedness companion to
the quantitative Lipschitz bound. The fixed energies enter only through the constant
denominator `Ei - Ej` (division by a constant, including `0`, is continuous in
mathlib), so no nonvanishing hypothesis is required.
type: ∀ (Ei Ej : ℝ), Continuous fun p ↦ CflibsFormal.twoLineBeta p.1 p.2 Ei Ej

name: CflibsFormal.twoLineBeta_stable
docstring:
**Temperature stability.** The two-line inverse-temperature (slope) estimate is
Lipschitz in the measured ordinates with explicit constant `2/|Eᵢ-Eⱼ|`: perturbing
each ordinate by at most `ε` changes the estimate by at most `2·ε/|Eᵢ-Eⱼ|`. The
bound is sharp (attained with opposite-sign perturbations), and `hEi` is
load-bearing for the nonzero denominator.
type:
∀ {yi yj yiHat yjHat Ei Ej eps : ℝ},
  Ei ≠ Ej →
    |yiHat - yi| ≤ eps →
      |yjHat - yj| ≤ eps →
        |CflibsFormal.twoLineBeta yiHat yjHat Ei Ej - CflibsFormal.twoLineBeta yi yj Ei Ej| ≤
          (2 : ℝ) * eps / |Ei - Ej|

name: CflibsFormal.twoLineBeta_stable_sharp
docstring:
**Sharpness of the temperature bound.** The Lipschitz constant `2/|Eᵢ−Eⱼ|` of
`twoLineBeta_stable` is attained: with the opposite-sign perturbations `yi ↦ yi − ε`,
`yj ↦ yj + ε` (each of size `ε`), the slope estimate changes by EXACTLY `2·ε/|Eᵢ−Eⱼ|`. So
the bound cannot be improved — the worst case is real, not a loose over-estimate.
type:
∀ {yi yj Ei Ej eps : ℝ},
  Ei ≠ Ej →
    (0 : ℝ) ≤ eps →
      |CflibsFormal.twoLineBeta (yi - eps) (yj + eps) Ei Ej -
            CflibsFormal.twoLineBeta yi yj Ei Ej| =
        (2 : ℝ) * eps / |Ei - Ej|

name: CflibsFormal.twoLine_boltzmannDesign_injective_of_hEdist
docstring:
**The n-line map generalizes the two-line result on the same nondegeneracy.** The
distinct-energy hypothesis `hEdist : p.E (emitA s₀) ≠ p.E (emitB s₀)` that powers
`JointIdentifiability.joint_identifiability` (it is what lets `observe₂` deliver the temperature
ratio at `s₀`) is *exactly* the condition making the two-line Boltzmann design map injective. So
the linear n-line identifiability of this module and the two-line joint identifiability rest on
one and the same nondegeneracy — the n-line design map at `n = 2` is the linear (Boltzmann-plot)
shadow of `observe₂` on the distinct-energy pair.
type:
∀ {species : Type u_1} {levelIndex : Type u_2} {emitA emitB : species → levelIndex}
  {p : CflibsFormal.PlasmaParams species levelIndex} (s₀ : species),
  p.E (emitA s₀) ≠ p.E (emitB s₀) →
    Function.Injective fun θ ↦
      (CflibsFormal.boltzmannDesign ![p.E (emitA s₀), p.E (emitB s₀)]).mulVec θ

name: CflibsFormal.twoLine_design_injective_of_distinct
docstring:
**Two-line design injectivity from a distinct-energy pair.** At `n = 2` the design map for
energies `(EA, EB)` is injective as soon as `EA ≠ EB`. This is the `n`-line map specialized to two
lines.
type:
∀ {EA EB : ℝ},
  EA ≠ EB → Function.Injective fun θ ↦ (CflibsFormal.boltzmannDesign ![EA, EB]).mulVec θ

name: CflibsFormal.twoStageTotal_ipd_gauge
docstring:
**Two-stage totals are unchanged.** With neutral density `N_I` of species `s`, the total
`N_I·(1 + S_s/n_e)` computed by the depression-free inverse (unlowered `χ_s`, density estimate
from the reference element) equals the total computed with the lowered energy and the true
`n_e`. The statement is for one species; `composition_ipd_gauge` applies it to all species at
once. An immediate consequence of `sahaRatio_ipd_gauge`, with its hypothesis and its scope
(REDUCED; published REDUCED).
type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ι] {κ : Type u_2} [inst_1 : Fintype κ] {ι' : Type u_3}
  {κ' : Type u_4} [inst_2 : Fintype ι'] [inst_3 : Fintype κ'] {kB T me h chim chis d Rm ne : ℝ}
  {gZ EZ : ι → ℝ} {gZ1 EZ1 : κ → ℝ} {gS ES : ι' → ℝ} {gS1 ES1 : κ' → ℝ} (NI : ℝ),
  Rm ≠ (0 : ℝ) →
    Rm * ne = CflibsFormal.sahaFactor kB T me h (chim - d) gZ EZ gZ1 EZ1 →
      NI *
          ((1 : ℝ) +
            CflibsFormal.sahaFactor kB T me h chis gS ES gS1 ES1 /
              CflibsFormal.electronDensityFromRatio kB T me h chim gZ EZ gZ1 EZ1 Rm) =
        NI * ((1 : ℝ) + CflibsFormal.sahaFactor kB T me h (chis - d) gS ES gS1 ES1 / ne)

name: CflibsFormal.two_level_balance
docstring:
**Two-level balance fixed point** (`REDUCED`; Griem 1997 §6). In steady state the collisional
excitation `n₁ R₁₂` balances collisional de-excitation plus radiative decay `n₂ (R₂₁ + A₂₁)`
(`hbal`); the LTE detailed-balance identity `n₁ R₁₂ = n₂ᴸᵀᴱ R₂₁` (`hlte`) *presumes the lower
level is itself thermalized*, `b₁ ≈ 1` — the standard two-level assumption. Their quotient is the
departure coefficient: `n₂/n₂ᴸᵀᴱ = R₂₁/(R₂₁ + A₂₁)`. This is a *departure* statement, not a claim
that LTE holds. `REDUCED`: the two-level reduction of the full collisional–radiative system.
type:
∀ {n1 n2 n2LTE R12 R21 A21 : ℝ},
  n1 * R12 = n2 * (R21 + A21) →
    n1 * R12 = n2LTE * R21 →
      n2LTE ≠ (0 : ℝ) → R21 + A21 ≠ (0 : ℝ) → n2 / n2LTE = CflibsFormal.departureCoeff R21 A21

name: CflibsFormal.two_ratio_diff
docstring: The two-line intensity-ratio difference is a scaled `Real.exp` difference.
type:
∀ {kB Fcal T T0 : ℝ} {g E A : Fin (2 : ℕ) → ℝ},
  (∀ (k : Fin (2 : ℕ)), (0 : ℝ) < g k) →
    (0 : ℝ) < Fcal →
      (∀ (k : Fin (2 : ℕ)), (0 : ℝ) < A k) →
        CflibsFormal.lineIntensity kB T (1 : ℝ) Fcal g E A (1 : Fin (2 : ℕ)) /
              CflibsFormal.lineIntensity kB T (1 : ℝ) Fcal g E A (0 : Fin (2 : ℕ)) -
            CflibsFormal.lineIntensity kB T0 (1 : ℝ) Fcal g E A (1 : Fin (2 : ℕ)) /
              CflibsFormal.lineIntensity kB T0 (1 : ℝ) Fcal g E A (0 : Fin (2 : ℕ)) =
          g (1 : Fin (2 : ℕ)) * A (1 : Fin (2 : ℕ)) / (g (0 : Fin (2 : ℕ)) * A (0 : Fin (2 : ℕ))) *
            (Real.exp ((E (0 : Fin (2 : ℕ)) - E (1 : Fin (2 : ℕ))) / (kB * T)) -
              Real.exp ((E (0 : Fin (2 : ℕ)) - E (1 : Fin (2 : ℕ))) / (kB * T0)))

name: CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM
docstring:
**Voigt FWHM (Olivero–Longbothum 1977).** The empirical combination of the Lorentzian width
`wL` (Stark + natural) and the Gaussian width `wG` (Doppler + instrument):
`w_V = 0.5346·w_L + √(0.2166·w_L² + w_G²)`.
type: ℝ → ℝ → ℝ

name: CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM_ge_gauss
docstring:
**The OL Voigt FWHM is at least the Gaussian width:** `w_G ≤ w_V` (a statement about the
fit formula `voigtFWHM`, not about the true Voigt profile).
type: ∀ {wL wG : ℝ}, (0 : ℝ) ≤ wL → (0 : ℝ) ≤ wG → wG ≤ CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM wL wG

name: CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM_ge_lorentz
docstring:
**The OL Voigt FWHM is at least the Lorentzian width:** `w_L ≤ w_V` (a statement about the
fit formula `voigtFWHM`, not about the true Voigt profile). Uses that
`0.5346 + √0.2166 ≥ 1` (the OL coefficients satisfy `√0.2166 > 0.4654 = 1 − 0.5346`).
type: ∀ {wL wG : ℝ}, (0 : ℝ) ≤ wL → wL ≤ CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM wL wG

name: CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM_ge_max
docstring:
**Lower sandwich rail (proved outright).** The OL Voigt FWHM is at least the larger of the two
component widths: `max(w_G, w_L) ≤ voigtFWHM w_L w_G`. Assembled from the two `VoigtWidth` lower
bounds `voigtFWHM_ge_gauss` and `voigtFWHM_ge_lorentz`.
type: ∀ {wL wG : ℝ}, (0 : ℝ) ≤ wL → (0 : ℝ) ≤ wG → Max.max wG wL ≤ CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM wL wG

name: CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM_le_olUpper
docstring:
**Sharp upper rail (proved outright).** By subadditivity of `√` on the two squared terms,
`voigtFWHM w_L w_G ≤ (0.5346 + √0.2166)·w_L + w_G`. The coefficient `0.5346 + √0.2166 = 1.00000305…`
is just above `1`, which is exactly why the naive rail `w_L + w_G` fails (see
`voigtFWHM_naive_upper_false`).
type:
∀ {wL wG : ℝ},
  (0 : ℝ) ≤ wL → (0 : ℝ) ≤ wG → CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM wL wG ≤ (0.5346 + √0.2166) * wL + wG

name: CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM_mono_wG
docstring: The Voigt FWHM is increasing in the Gaussian width `wG`.
type:
∀ {wL wG₁ wG₂ : ℝ},
  (0 : ℝ) ≤ wG₁ → wG₁ ≤ wG₂ → CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM wL wG₁ ≤ CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM wL wG₂

name: CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM_mono_wL
docstring: The Voigt FWHM is increasing in the Lorentzian width `wL`.
type:
∀ {wG wL₁ wL₂ : ℝ},
  (0 : ℝ) ≤ wL₁ → wL₁ ≤ wL₂ → CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM wL₁ wG ≤ CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM wL₂ wG

name: CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM_naive_upper_false
docstring:
**Real finding (proved).** The *naive* upper rail `voigtFWHM ≤ w_L + w_G` is FALSE. Witness:
`(w_L, w_G) = (1, 0)` gives `voigtFWHM 1 0 = 0.5346 + √0.2166 > 1 = w_L + w_G`, because
`√0.2166 > 0.4654` (as `0.4654² = 0.21659716 < 0.2166`). This is why the honest enclosure width
carries the `η·w_L` correction rather than the textbook `min(fG,fL)`.
type: ¬∀ (wL wG : ℝ), (0 : ℝ) ≤ wL → (0 : ℝ) ≤ wG → CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM wL wG ≤ wL + wG

name: CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM_pos
docstring:
The Voigt FWHM is strictly positive when there is a nonzero Gaussian width (always true in
practice — thermal Doppler — for `wL ≥ 0`).
type: ∀ {wL wG : ℝ}, (0 : ℝ) ≤ wL → (0 : ℝ) < wG → (0 : ℝ) < CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM wL wG

name: CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM_true_enclosure
docstring:
**Conditional error enclosure (main result).** Let `Ftrue` be the true convolution Voigt FWHM,
bracketed by the standard *uncited* bounds `hlo : max(w_G, w_L) ≤ Ftrue`, `hhi : Ftrue ≤ w_L + w_G`
(taken as hypotheses, not proved here).
Since the OL value also satisfies `max(w_G,w_L) ≤ voigtFWHM w_L w_G ≤ (0.5346+√0.2166)·w_L + w_G`,
both `voigtFWHM w_L w_G` and `Ftrue` live in that common interval, so
`|voigtFWHM w_L w_G − Ftrue| ≤ min(w_G, w_L) + η·w_L` with `η = 0.5346 + √0.2166 − 1 > 0`.
Non-circular: `Ftrue` is abstract and independent of the OL formula; the bound is `0` only when
`w_L = 0` (pure Gaussian, where OL is exact).
type:
∀ {wL wG Ftrue : ℝ},
  (0 : ℝ) ≤ wL →
    (0 : ℝ) ≤ wG →
      Max.max wG wL ≤ Ftrue →
        Ftrue ≤ wL + wG →
          |CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM wL wG - Ftrue| ≤ Min.min wG wL + (0.5346 + √0.2166 - (1 : ℝ)) * wL

name: CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM_true_enclosure_clean
docstring:
**Clean-constant enclosure.** The same bound with a fully rational width: since
`√0.2166 < 0.46541`, the correction `η = 0.5346 + √0.2166 − 1 < 10⁻⁵`, giving
`|voigtFWHM w_L w_G − Ftrue| ≤ min(w_G, w_L) + 10⁻⁵·w_L`. This is the width of the assumed
bracket, not the accuracy of the fit: at `w_L = w_G` it is about 61% of the Voigt width.
type:
∀ {wL wG Ftrue : ℝ},
  (0 : ℝ) ≤ wL →
    (0 : ℝ) ≤ wG →
      Max.max wG wL ≤ Ftrue →
        Ftrue ≤ wL + wG → |CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM wL wG - Ftrue| ≤ Min.min wG wL + 1e-5 * wL

name: CflibsFormal.voigt_gaussian_limit
docstring:
**Pure-Gaussian limit (exact).** With no Lorentzian broadening, the Voigt FWHM is exactly the
Gaussian width: `w_V = w_G` at `w_L = 0`.
type: ∀ {wG : ℝ}, (0 : ℝ) ≤ wG → CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM (0 : ℝ) wG = wG

name: CflibsFormal.voigt_lorentzian_limit
docstring:
**Pure-Lorentzian limit (honest restatement).** With no Gaussian broadening,
`w_V = (0.5346 + √0.2166)·w_L`. Because `0.5346 + √0.2166 = 1.00000305… ≠ 1`, this is **not**
exactly
`w_L`: the OL formula misses the Lorentzian limit by a relative `3·10⁻⁶`.
type: ∀ {wL : ℝ}, (0 : ℝ) ≤ wL → CflibsFormal.voigtFWHM wL (0 : ℝ) = (0.5346 + √0.2166) * wL

name: CflibsFormal.wMean
docstring:
**Weighted mean** `Ē_w = (∑_k w k * E k) / ∑_k w k` of the upper-level energies `E` with line
weights `w` (in the noise reading, `w k = 1/σ_k²`, the inverse variance of line `k`'s ordinate).
Totalized division: `0` when `∑ w = 0`, which positive weights on a non-empty line set exclude.
type: {ι : Type u_1} → [Fintype ι] → (ι → ℝ) → (ι → ℝ) → ℝ

name: CflibsFormal.wSS
docstring:
**Weighted centred sum of squares** `wSS = ∑_k w k * (E k − Ē_w)²`, the weighted energy
spread of the Boltzmann plot. With `w k = 1/σ_k²` it is the information about the slope
carried by the line set; for unit weights it is the usual `SS_E`.
type: {ι : Type u_1} → [Fintype ι] → (ι → ℝ) → (ι → ℝ) → ℝ

name: CflibsFormal.weighted_mean_strict_between
docstring:
Pure-algebra mediant lemma: a strictly positive weighted mean of two *distinct* reals
lies strictly between them — in particular it lies in their unordered interval and equals
neither. No orientation (`x < y` or `y < x`) is assumed.
type:
∀ {wa wb x y : ℝ},
  (0 : ℝ) < wa →
    (0 : ℝ) < wb →
      x ≠ y →
        (wa * x + wb * y) / (wa + wb) ∈ Set.uIcc x y ∧
          (wa * x + wb * y) / (wa + wb) ≠ x ∧ (wa * x + wb * y) / (wa + wb) ≠ y

name: CflibsFormal.withinCross
docstring:
**Weighted within-group cross product.**
`withinCross grp w x y = ∑_k w k * (x k − x̄_{grp k}) * (y k − ȳ_{grp k})`, where `x̄_e`, `ȳ_e` are
the weighted group means (`gMean`). This is the numerator of the fixed-effects (element-dummy)
least-squares slope: each line is centred on the mean of its own group, so any per-group intercept
drops out.
type:
{ι : Type u_1} →
  {κ : Type u_2} → [Fintype ι] → [DecidableEq κ] → (ι → κ) → (ι → ℝ) → (ι → ℝ) → (ι → ℝ) → ℝ

name: CflibsFormal.withinSS
docstring:
**Weighted within-group sum of squares** `SS_W = ∑_k w k * (x k − x̄_{grp k})²`, i.e.
`withinCross grp w x x`. It is the denominator of the fixed-effects slope and, with positive
weights, it vanishes exactly when `x` is constant on every group.
type: {ι : Type u_1} → {κ : Type u_2} → [Fintype ι] → [DecidableEq κ] → (ι → κ) → (ι → ℝ) → (ι → ℝ) → ℝ

name: CflibsFormal.wlsWeight
docstring:
**Weighted-least-squares slope weight** `ω_k = w k * (E k − Ē_w) / wSS`. The linear estimator
`∑_k ω_k * y k` is the weighted-RSS-minimizing slope (the one-group case of `feSlope` /
`feSlope_isMin`, whose group mean `gMean` reduces to `wMean` by `gMean_const_eq_wMean`); the
identification of the slopes is not proved in this file. For unit weights this is the
OLS weight `(E k − Ē)/SS_E` (`CflibsFormal.olsWeight`). Totalized division: `0` when
`wSS = 0`.
type: {ι : Type u_1} → [Fintype ι] → (ι → ℝ) → (ι → ℝ) → ι → ℝ

name: CflibsFormal.wls_min_noiseGain
docstring:
**WLS attains the minimum noise gain among linear unbiased slope estimators.**
Let `a : ι → ℝ` be the weights of any linear slope estimator `∑_k a k * y k` that is unbiased for
every straight line `y k = α + β * E k`, i.e. `∑_k a k = 0` and `∑_k a k * E k = 1`. Its noise
gain under per-line variances `σ_k² = 1/w k` is `∑_k a k² / w k`. The theorem says:
0. the WLS weights are themselves linear-unbiased (`∑ ω = 0`, `∑ ω E = 1`),
1. the WLS weights `wlsWeight w E` have noise gain exactly `1 / wSS w E`, and
2. every unbiased `a` has noise gain at least `1 / wSS w E`.
So `1 / wSS` is the floor, and WLS attains it. Under uncorrelated ordinate noise with
`Var ε_k = 1/w k` this is the deterministic core of "WLS is the best linear unbiased slope
estimator" (Aitken); the variance statement itself is a separate target.

This is a BLUE floor, not a Cramér–Rao bound: it compares linear unbiased estimators only, and
no Fisher information is involved.

Hypotheses.
* `hw : ∀ k, 0 < w k`: finite positive variances `1/w k`; the noise gain divides by `w k`, and
  both the equality and the inequality use `w k > 0`. Item 0 uses it for `∑ w > 0`, so that
  the weighted deviations `w k * (E k − Ē_w)` sum to zero.
* `ha0 : ∑ a = 0`, `ha1 : ∑ a E = 1`: unbiasedness for every intercept and slope.
* `hSS : 0 < wSS w E`: the slope is identifiable. Given `hw`, `ha0` and `ha1` it is in fact
  implied (if `wSS = 0` then every `E k = Ē_w`, so `∑ a E = Ē_w * ∑ a = 0 ≠ 1`); it is kept to
  name the identifiability condition and to save the prover that derivation.

Scope: relation PURE-MATH; no physics definition is used; published PURE-MATH. Physics reading
(REDUCED, not part of the statement): Boltzmann-plot ordinates `y k = log (I k/(g k A k))` with
uncorrelated additive noise of known variance `σ_k² = 1/w k`. Atomic-data (`gA`) uncertainties
are a bias, not noise, and should not enter `w`.

Literature: Aitken 1935 (Proc. Roy. Soc. Edinburgh 55, 42) for generalized least squares;
Tognoni et al. 2010 (Spectrochim. Acta B 65, 1) for the CF-LIBS uncertainty context.
type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ι] {w E a : ι → ℝ},
  (∀ (k : ι), (0 : ℝ) < w k) →
    (0 : ℝ) < CflibsFormal.wSS w E →
      ∑ k, a k = (0 : ℝ) →
        ∑ k, a k * E k = (1 : ℝ) →
          (∑ k, CflibsFormal.wlsWeight w E k = (0 : ℝ) ∧
              ∑ k, CflibsFormal.wlsWeight w E k * E k = (1 : ℝ)) ∧
            ∑ k, CflibsFormal.wlsWeight w E k ^ (2 : ℕ) / w k = (1 : ℝ) / CflibsFormal.wSS w E ∧
              (1 : ℝ) / CflibsFormal.wSS w E ≤ ∑ k, a k ^ (2 : ℕ) / w k

name: CflibsFormal.wrong_weight_detected
docstring:
**Detection power.** Suppose both measured ordinates are within their error bars of the
common true value `y`, but line `j` is then read with a `g·A` off by the factor `c`, which
moves its ordinate to `yj − log c` (`ordinate_gap_of_wrong_weight`). If
`|log c| > 2·(εj + εk)` the gate fails. Sufficient, not necessary.
type:
∀ {y yj yk εj εk c : ℝ},
  |yj - y| ≤ εj →
    |yk - y| ≤ εk →
      (2 : ℝ) * (εj + εk) < |Real.log c| →
        ¬CflibsFormal.SharedLevelConsistent (yj - Real.log c) yk εj εk

name: CflibsFormal.zoneBeta
docstring: Zone `z`'s inverse temperature `b z = 1/(k_B T_z)`, the Laplace abscissa.
type: {ζ : Type u_1} → ℝ → (ζ → ℝ) → ζ → ℝ

name: CflibsFormal.zoneWeight
docstring:
Zone `z`'s Boltzmann-plot mass `w z = Fcal · N z / U(T_z)`: its partition-normalized,
calibration-absorbed column density. `∑ z, zoneWeight …` is the quantity the intercept
bounds from below.
type:
{ζ : Type u_1} →
  {ι : Type u_2} → [Fintype ι] → ℝ → ℝ → (ζ → ℝ) → (ζ → ℝ) → (ι → ℝ) → (ι → ℝ) → ζ → ℝ

name: CflibsFormal.zoneWeight_pos
docstring: Zone masses are positive, so the mixture machinery applies.
type:
∀ {ζ : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] {kB Fcal : ℝ} {T N : ζ → ℝ}
  {g E : ι → ℝ},
  (∀ (k : ι), (0 : ℝ) < g k) →
    (∀ (z : ζ), (0 : ℝ) < N z) →
      (0 : ℝ) < Fcal → ∀ (z : ζ), (0 : ℝ) < CflibsFormal.zoneWeight kB Fcal T N g E z
